audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text says "his Q shield and passive don't save him from your E knock-up + W tick + Q slow". That is the exact reverse of what those two abilities do to Zac specifically, and it is the only place either is mentioned.
audit.why: Void Stone (P): "Kassadin takes reduced magic damage." Null Sphere (Q): "The excess energy forms around himself, granting a temporary shield that absorbs magic damage." Zac's damage is magic — Unstable Matter is explicitly "a percentage of their maximum health as magic damage". So Kassadin's passive and his shield are both targeted mitigation against everything Zac does, and the entry tells the player they are irrelevant. This is the most likely explanation for a 47.52% win rate sitting under an entry that reads like a free lane.
audit.corrected: Void Stone reduces magic damage and Null Sphere shields against magic — your whole kit is magic, so commit fully instead of chipping.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags this entry for having no cooldown sequencing, and every piece of guidance it does give is built on waiting out Riftwalk: winCon "Slingshot him on the Riftwalk cooldown", dosFull[0] "Only engage once it is down or baited", dosFull[1] "E from fog when Riftwalk is down", breakdown.mid "when it is down, run your full pattern".
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 and 2s at rank 3. There is no window in which it is down for long enough to matter, so the entire sequencing model of this entry describes something that does not happen. What actually gates it is mana: Riot's text says "Multiple Riftwalks in a short period of time cost additional Mana", on a champion with a 40-mana base cost. The punishable state is a drained pool after repeat blinks, not a cooldown.
audit.corrected: Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 and 2s at rank 3 — you never catch it down. Punish the escalating mana cost of repeat blinks instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: Force Pulse is never mentioned in either layer, and neither is the fact that Zac's own casting charges it.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Kassadin draws energy from spells cast in his vicinity. Upon charging up, Kassadin can use Force Pulse." Any spell cast near him counts, including Zac's. Unstable Matter is on a flat 5s cooldown and is the ability a Zac player is most likely to hold down while standing next to someone — so idling next to Kassadin spamming W is actively arming his slow. This is the kind of detail that only shows up when you read the passive charging condition rather than the damage numbers.
audit.corrected: Force Pulse charges off spells cast near him — your 5s W feeds it, so cast it inside a commit rather than idling next to him.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content chart gives Zac all 7 stages while Zac wins only 47.52% over 141 games — and the entry's own late and spikes[3] text says Kassadin outscales and the lane is about ending early.
audit.why: Every stage after the lane phase belongs to Kassadin: his first AP item plus the mana to sustain Riftwalk is his spike, his carry rating in this very entry is 9.5/10, and his passive plus Null Sphere shield only get better against Zac's magic damage as the game goes on. Zac keeps levels 1-5, which is where his kill pressure genuinely exists.
audit.corrected: Zac / Zac / Zac / Zac / Skill / Kassadin / Kassadin.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nether Blade is never mentioned, so Kassadin's burst has no stated tell.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Kassadin's next basic attack deals significant bonus magic damage and restores Mana." It is an attack reset on a 7s cooldown and _missing-interactions.json flags it as the burst tell for this matchup — and the mana restore is also part of why his pool recovers between Riftwalks.
audit.corrected: Nether Blade's wind-up is the burst tell, and it also refunds him mana.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing notes that Kassadin ignores unit collision.
audit.why: Void Stone: "Kassadin takes reduced magic damage and ignores unit collision." Walking him into your own minions to slow an escape does not work, which matters when the plan is a gank set-up or a dive — the standard body-blocking that helps against most melee laners is off the table.
audit.corrected: He ignores unit collision, so minions will not body-block him for a gank.

notes:
WORTH VERIFYING ON THE WIKI, not asserted anywhere in my text: Riot describes Null Sphere as "dealing damage and interrupting channels", and Zac's Elastic Slingshot is a charge-up. If Null Sphere interrupts a charging Slingshot, that is a decisive lane interaction and belongs in this entry — but Zac's kit file carries no "channel" flag and nothing in the kit files establishes it either way, so I left it out rather than guess.

The corrected win[] chart moves the last three stages to Kassadin, which finally agrees with the entry's OWN prose: late already says "Kassadin outscales the game late, so the lane was always about ending early" and spikes[3] says "Late Kassadin outscales everyone". A chart giving Zac 7 of 7 contradicted the text sitting next to it as well as the 47.52% win rate.

The full layer's phases[].side reads Zac / Zac / Zac / Zac / Skill / Zac / Zac and is equally wrong at the item stages, but side values are under the applier's 12-character minimum for a full-layer "before" and cannot be proposed.
